args.body:
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Concession Agreement — TxDOT Counterparty Markup
Energy & Natural Resources
Matter File 13 — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement
Output: redline-review-memorandum.docx

CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This memorandum compares the Texas Department of Transportation ("TxDOT") markup of the Concession Agreement against our original draft and negotiation playbook, cross-referencing the lender side letter, surety comfort letter, and project financial model. We reconcile every identified deviation against the base materials, disclosure schedules, and Exhibit B survival matrix. Misfiled administrative correspondence in the matter folder (unrelated engagement) was disregarded.

TxDOT's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap and conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (2) Expansion of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs to exclude regulatory action of the type already disclosed and at issue on this project; and
  (3) A new contractual limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest deal-team correspondence): the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not followed herein.

Risk summary (see § IV for full ratings):

  • Indemnification cap reduction .............. HIGH
  • Basket conversion (deductible → tipping) ... LOW (client will concede)
  • MAE regulatory-action carve-outs ........... HIGH
  • Survival / limitation-period shortening .... CRITICAL (walk-away)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base / firm materials
  • Original draft Concession Agreement and firm negotiation playbook
    (Matter File 13 — Deal materials)
  • Key provisions framework: representations and warranties, covenants,
    conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination

Counterparty paper
  • TxDOT markup (Counterparty markup — energy-natural-resources)

Schedules and exhibits (control over general base statements)
  • Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the
    markup's MAE carve-outs
  • Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification
    changes would silently reallocate
  • Exhibit B — survival matrix contradicted by the markup's limitation-
    period change

Cross-references
  • Lender side letter (financing conditions tied to indemnity package,
    MAE definition, and representation survival)
  • Surety comfort / bond letter (penal-sum and indemnity alignment;
    survival of core contractor/concessionaire reps)
  • Project financial model (contingency, indemnity recovery assumptions,
    and DSCR sensitivity to uncapped or reduced recovery)

Deal-team direction
  • Partner email thread — latest message controls: concede basket
    conversion; survival-period reduction is walk-away

Excluded
  • Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 13 (misfiled; different
    client engagement; not relied upon)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base draft / playbook
  Firm-standard bilateral indemnification cap sized to the transaction
  economics and aligned with Schedule 5.2 retained-liability architecture.
  Playbook position: maintain cap at negotiated baseline; any reduction
  requires express client approval and model re-run.

TxDOT markup
  Cap is reduced without a corresponding blackline call-out or footnote
  explaining the quantum or rationale ("silent" reduction).

Schedule / exhibit interaction
  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. A lower cap would silently shift
  residual exposure on those retained items back to the concessionaire /
  our client once the reduced cap is exhausted, undermining the bargained
  risk allocation.

Lender / surety / model cross-reference
  • Lender letter conditions draw and ongoing availability on an indemnity
    package no less favorable than the draft shared at commitment. A silent
    cap cut is a financing-condition defect and may require lender consent
    or a MAC/MAE-style re-underwrite.
  • Surety letter assumes indemnity capacity consistent with the original
    cap when sizing penal sum and co-indemnitor exposure.
  • Financial model books expected indemnity recovery and contingency
    against the original cap. Cap reduction degrades recovery assumptions
    and can pressure DSCR / lock-up tests under downside cases.

Risk rating: HIGH

Disposition: REJECT the silent cap reduction. Require restoration of the
original cap (or an expressly negotiated alternative quantum with model
and lender/surety sign-off).

Counter-proposal language
  "Section [Indemnification — Cap]. The aggregate liability of the
  Indemnifying Party under this Article shall not exceed the Cap Amount
  equal to [ORIGINAL CAP AMOUNT / __% of the aggregate Concession Fee /
  Enterprise Value], which Cap Amount shall not be reduced, eroded, or
  re-characterized except by written amendment executed by the Parties
  and, to the extent required under the Financing Documents, consented to
  by the Lenders. For the avoidance of doubt, no markup, schedule update,
  or side letter shall be construed to amend the Cap Amount unless it
  expressly identifies this Section and states the revised Cap Amount in
  numerals and words. Liabilities described on Schedule 5.2 shall continue
  to be treated in accordance with that Schedule and shall not be deemed
  absorbed into, or limited by, any reduction of the Cap Amount."

Optional fallback (only if client later authorizes limited movement)
  Restore original cap for (i) title, authority, and fundamental reps,
  (ii) Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, (iii) fraud and willful
  misconduct, and (iv) environmental / regulatory indemnity; permit a
  modest reduction solely for general operational indemnities, subject to
  lender and surety written confirmation and an updated model run.


DEVIATION 2 — Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base draft / playbook
  Deductible basket: indemnitor pays only amounts in excess of the basket
  threshold. Playbook preference is deductible to avoid first-dollar
  claims administration and to keep de minimis noise out of the indemnity
  channel.

TxDOT markup
  Converts the basket to a tipping (threshold) basket: once claims in the
  aggregate exceed the threshold, recovery is from dollar one.

Schedule / exhibit interaction
  Interacts with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities (claim aggregation and
  what counts toward the basket). Does not, by itself, reallocate the
  Schedule 5.2 items, but a tipping structure increases expected recovery
  velocity on covered claims once the threshold is crossed.

Lender / surety / model cross-reference
  • Lender package is generally neutral to deductible vs. tipping if the
    threshold quantum is unchanged; primary lender sensitivity is the cap
    and survival, not basket mechanics.
  • Surety exposure is modestly affected (earlier first-dollar payout
    dynamics) but typically not a consent item at this threshold.
  • Model: tipping basket slightly improves expected indemnity recovery
    NPV versus deductible; not material to base-case DSCR.

Risk rating: LOW

Disposition: CONCEDE per controlling client instruction (latest deal-team
correspondence). Document the concession expressly so it cannot be paired
with the cap cut or survival cut as a "package" takeaway.

Counter-proposal / acceptance language
  "Section [Indemnification — Basket]. The Parties agree that the
  Indemnification Basket shall operate as a tipping basket: no
  indemnification shall be payable until the aggregate of all Claims
  exceeds the Basket Amount of $[___], and thereafter the Indemnifying
  Party shall be liable for the full amount of such Claims from the first
  dollar (subject to the Cap Amount and any other express limitations in
  this Article). This concession is limited to basket mechanics only and
  shall not be construed as agreement to any reduction of the Cap Amount,
  any change to survival periods under Exhibit B, or any expansion of MAE
  carve-outs."


DEVIATION 3 — MAE Definition: New Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base draft / playbook
  MAE definition follows firm energy/infrastructure precedent: material
  adverse effect on business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or
  results of operations of the Project / Concessionaire, taken as a whole,
  with standard carve-outs (general economic/market conditions, acts of
  war/terrorism, changes in law of general application, etc.) that
  re-include disproportionate effects on the Project. Playbook: do not
  carve out project-specific or disclosed regulatory actions that are the
  very risk the MAE condition and interim covenants are meant to police.

TxDOT markup
  Adds carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in
  this matter," which would exclude from MAE the category of regulatory
  events already in view on this concession.

Schedule / exhibit interaction
  Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect
  these carve-outs. If the carve-outs stand, adverse developments in those
  inquiries — including orders, penalties, permit suspensions, or scope
  restrictions — would be definitionally incapable of constituting an MAE,
  gutting the closing condition and related termination / walk rights tied
  to MAE. Scheduled exceptions control over general base statements; the
  correct structure is disclosure + bring-down against a clean MAE, not
  definitional erasure of the disclosed risk class.

Lender / surety / model cross-reference
  • Lender letter typically keys commitment conditions, drawdowns, and
    mandatory prepayment / default triggers to absence of MAE, using the
    agreement definition. Regulatory carve-outs of this breadth are a
    known lender objection and may force a parallel amendment to the
    credit MAE or a specific lender consent condition around Schedule 3.7
    matters.
  • Surety underwriting of performance / payment product assumes MAE-
    level off-ramps remain available if regulatory action impairs the
    work; broad carve-outs increase surety residual risk.
  • Financial model downside cases include regulatory-adverse paths tied
    to Schedule 3.7. Removing MAE coverage for those paths transfers
    unpriced downside to equity and may require re-sizing contingency or
    reserve accounts.

Risk rating: HIGH

Disposition: REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs as drafted. Preserve
MAE coverage for project-specific and Schedule 3.7 regulatory matters;
permit only ordinary-course, generally applicable regulatory carve-outs
with a disproportionate-impact back-door.

Counter-proposal language
  "Section [Definitions — Material Adverse Effect]. 'Material Adverse
  Effect' means any event, change, circumstance, occurrence, fact, or
  effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would
  reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the
  business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of
  operations of the Project or the Concessionaire, taken as a whole, or
  (b) the ability of a Party to consummate the transactions or perform
  its obligations under the Concession Documents; provided, that none of
  the following shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into
  account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse
  Effect: [standard general carve-outs — general economic or financial
  market conditions; changes in Law of general applicability; acts of
  God, war, terrorism; etc.], except, in each case, to the extent such
  event, change, circumstance, occurrence, fact, or effect has a
  disproportionate adverse effect on the Project or the Concessionaire
  relative to other similarly situated projects or operators.

  For the avoidance of doubt, (i) any development with respect to the
  matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7, (ii) any project-specific regulatory
  action, order, investigation, permit condition, or enforcement matter
  directed at the Project, the Concessionaire, or the Work, and (iii) any
  regulatory action that is not of general applicability to similarly
  situated projects in the State, shall not be excluded from the
  determination of Material Adverse Effect by reason of any carve-out in
  this definition."

Fallback (narrow, only if commercially necessary)
  Limited carve-out solely for the existence (but not the adverse
  development, expansion, or outcome) of the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries
  as disclosed as of the agreement date, with express re-inclusion of any
  material worsening, new orders, or scope expansion after signing.


DEVIATION 4 — Limitation Period Shortening Survival of Core Representations
────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Base draft / playbook
  Survival of representations tracks Exhibit B survival matrix: fundamental
  / core representations (authority, title/concession rights, capitalization
  / organization, brokers, and other fundamentals) survive for an extended
  period (or until expiration of the applicable statute of limitations);
  operational and general reps survive for a standard post-closing or post-
  appointed period. Playbook treats erosion of core-rep survival as
  non-market and non-negotiable without express C-suite / board authority.

TxDOT markup
  Inserts a new contractual limitation period that shortens survival for
  the core representations, directly contradicting Exhibit B.

Schedule / exhibit interaction
  Exhibit B is the controlling survival matrix. Scheduled exceptions and
  exhibits control over general statements in the base materials; the
  markup's limitation period cannot silently override Exhibit B. Any
  change must amend Exhibit B expressly, line by line.

Lender / surety / model cross-reference
  • Lender letter conditions and bring-down mechanics assume core reps
    remain live through the periods in Exhibit B (and often through final
    maturity for fundamental reps). Shortened survival is a financing-
    document inconsistency and a likely consent / amendment item.
  • Surety reliance on core contractor/concessionaire reps (authority,
    enforceability, no conflict, permits) for the life of the bond package
    is impaired if survival is cut short.
  • Model assumes post-closing indemnity recoveries on core-rep breaches
    remain available for the Exhibit B horizon; truncating survival
    reduces expected recovery and can affect reserve release timing.

Risk rating: CRITICAL (client walk-away)

Disposition: REJECT in full. Per controlling client instruction, any
survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. Do not trade survival for
basket, cap, or MAE movement.

Counter-proposal language
  "Section [Survival; Limitation Period]. The representations and
  warranties of the Parties shall survive the Appointed Date / Closing and
  remain in full force and effect for the periods set forth in Exhibit B
  (Survival Matrix), which Exhibit B is incorporated by reference and
  controls in the event of any conflict with this Section or any general
  limitation period. No general contractual limitation period, statute-of-
  limitations waiver, or similar provision shall shorten, limit, or
  extinguish the survival periods specified in Exhibit B for Fundamental
  Representations or other categories identified therein. Claims for
  breach of a representation or warranty may be asserted at any time
  prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period in Exhibit B,
  and any claim notice timely given shall preserve the claim until finally
  resolved. Fundamental Representations shall survive until the expiration
  of the applicable statute of limitations (or for the period stated in
  Exhibit B, if longer), and nothing in this Agreement shall be construed
  to impose a shorter bar."

Walk-away instruction (to be reflected in cover note / term sheet)
  If TxDOT insists on any reduction to Exhibit B survival for core /
  fundamental representations, counsel is instructed to escalate and,
  absent a revised client mandate, terminate negotiations on that issue
  rather than accept the cut.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. CONSOLIDATED RISK RATING TABLE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Item                         | Rating     | Client posture        | Action
-----------------------------|------------|-----------------------|---------------------------
Indemnification cap cut      | HIGH       | Resist / restore      | Reject; counter as § III.1
Basket: deductible→tipping   | LOW        | Concede               | Accept; cabin as § III.2
MAE regulatory carve-outs    | HIGH       | Resist; protect Sch. 3.7 | Reject; counter as § III.3
Survival / limitation period | CRITICAL   | Walk-away             | Reject; counter as § III.4; no trade

Composite negotiation posture: Accept basket conversion only as a
standalone concession. Hold firm on cap, MAE (Schedule 3.7), and Exhibit B
survival. Package any movement on cap quantum only with full lender and
surety written comfort and a refreshed model case; never package with
survival.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. CROSS-REFERENCE CHECKLIST (LENDER / SURETY / MODEL)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Lender side letter
  [ ] Confirm indemnity cap in Concession Agreement matches commitment-
      condition baseline; obtain written consent before any cap reduction.
  [ ] Confirm credit-agreement MAE definition remains aligned; reject
      regulatory carve-outs that desynchronize project MAE from credit MAE.
  [ ] Confirm representation survival / bring-down through Exhibit B
      periods; flag limitation-period markup as a consent item.
  [ ] Confirm basket mechanics change (tipping) is not a reserved matter
      under the financing documents (expected: not reserved).

Surety comfort / bond letter
  [ ] Reaffirm penal-sum and co-indemnitor assumptions against original
      cap and Exhibit B survival.
  [ ] Notify surety of proposed MAE regulatory carve-outs and obtain
      confirmation that bond underwriting is unchanged, or document
      increased surety conditions.
  [ ] Confirm no surety objection to tipping-basket concession.

Financial model
  [ ] Re-run downside cases with (a) reduced cap, (b) MAE unavailability
      on Schedule 3.7 paths, and (c) truncated core-rep survival; present
      DSCR / lock-up / contingency impacts to client before any commercial
      movement on HIGH items.
  [ ] Book basket-conversion (tipping) as a minor positive to expected
      recovery; no model blocker.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Transmit a marked counter-draft that:
   • Restores the original indemnification Cap Amount and adds anti-silent-
     amendment language (§ III.1);
   • Accepts tipping-basket mechanics with express isolation language
     (§ III.2);
   • Deletes TxDOT's regulatory-action MAE carve-outs and inserts the
     Schedule 3.7 / project-specific re-inclusion language (§ III.3);
   • Deletes the new limitation period insofar as it shortens Exhibit B
     survival and inserts controlling Exhibit B language (§ III.4).

2. Cover note to TxDOT counsel stating:
   • Basket conversion accepted as a gesture of movement;
   • Cap, MAE (including Schedule 3.7 matters), and Exhibit B survival are
     firm positions required by financing, surety, and board risk
     tolerances;
   • Survival reduction is non-negotiable.

3. Parallel outbound:
   • Lender counsel: summary of deviations and confirmation that our
     counter-draft preserves financing conditions;
   • Surety: same, with request for reaffirmation of comfort letter;
   • Client / sponsor model team: request refreshed downside cases only if
     TxDOT re-trades on HIGH items.

4. Internal: escalate immediately if TxDOT re-tables survival cuts; per
   controlling instruction, prepare walk-away path rather than accept.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. DEVIATION RECONCILIATION STATEMENT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Every deviation identified in the counterparty markup has been addressed:

  ✓ Indemnification cap silently reduced — analyzed; HIGH; rejected with
    counter-proposal; Schedule 5.2 and lender/surety/model impacts noted.
  ✓ Basket converted deductible → tipping — analyzed; LOW; conceded per
    latest client instruction; acceptance cabined so it cannot pull through
    cap or survival concessions.
  ✓ MAE regulatory-action carve-outs — analyzed; HIGH; rejected with
    counter-proposal; Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries expressly protected;
    lender/surety/model impacts noted.
  ✓ Limitation period shortening core-rep survival — analyzed; CRITICAL;
    rejected as walk-away; Exhibit B reaffirmed as controlling; lender/
    surety/model impacts noted.

No reliance was placed on misfiled unrelated administrative correspondence
in the matter folder.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VIII. CLOSING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

We recommend issuing the counter-draft and cover note described in § VI
promptly, with concurrent lender and surety touchpoints. Please advise if
the client revises the walk-away posture on survival or authorizes limited
fallback movement on the indemnification cap quantum after model and
financing review.

Respectfully submitted,
Energy & Natural Resources — Deal Team
Matter File 13 — Concession Agreement TxDOT Markup Review

[END OF MEMORANDUM]
